problem: LLMs struggle to efficiently handle software engineering tasks that require both reasoning-intensive planning and adaptive multi-turn agent interactions.
approach: Combines agentless training with structured skill priors (localization, code editing, reflection) to enable efficient SWE-agent adaptation, using public trajectories and workflow-based single-turn verification.
contribution: Achieves 60.4% on SWE-bench Verified among workflow approaches, and 48.6% pass@1 with SFT adaptation, matching Claude 3.5 Sonnet performance.

problem: Causal discovery from observational data is underdetermined; recovering unique causal graphs requires auxiliary information and assumptions.
approach: Leverages structural causal model distributions with data from multiple environments differing in noise statistics, connecting causal discovery to nonlinear ICA via duality.
contribution: First result guaranteeing entire causal graph recovery with constant number of environments (two suffice) and arbitrary nonlinear mechanisms under Gaussianity.

problem: Positive-Unlabeled learning research lacks standardized benchmarks, leading to irreproducible findings and unsubstantiated performance claims.
approach: Introduces unified data generation, integrated framework of 18 state-of-the-art PU methods, and standardized protocols enabling 2880 systematic evaluations.
contribution: Reveals performance landscape with critical trade-offs between effectiveness and efficiency, and maps method robustness across label frequencies and selection bias conditions.

problem: Vision-Language-Action models' performance critically depends on underlying VLMs, yet this choice and capability impact remain poorly understood.
approach: VLM4VLA pipeline converts general-purpose VLMs to VLA policies with minimal adaptation, enabling fair comparison across architectures and systematic analysis of embodied capabilities.
contribution: Demonstrates VLM general capabilities poorly predict downstream task performance; fine-tuning vision encoders is critical, and specific embodied skill improvements don't guarantee better control.

problem: Multimodal LLMs hallucinate audiovisual cues and learn spurious associations between emotions and irrelevant audiovisual signals.
approach: Introduces EmoReAlM benchmark for measuring hallucinations and cue-emotion associations; proposes AVEm-DPO using preference optimization with regularization penalizing text prior reliance.
contribution: Achieves 6-19% relative performance improvement on DFEW, RAVDESS, and EMER benchmarks in zero-shot settings.

problem: LLM-powered agents assume tool executions always succeed and lack nuanced understanding of tool performance boundaries, introducing planning uncertainty in complex domains like visual content generation.
approach: PerfGuard framework models tool performance via multi-dimensional scoring, dynamically adapts tool selection by comparing theoretical vs actual rankings, and optimizes planning to align with performance-aware strategies.
contribution: Improves tool selection accuracy, execution reliability, and user intent alignment over state-of-the-art methods in AIGC tasks.

problem: Generative diffusion models struggle to align learned distributions with real data, creating inevitable gaps between generated and real data.
approach: Weak-to-Strong Diffusion uses estimated gaps between weak and strong models to guide latent variables toward real data distribution via alternating denoising and inversion.
contribution: Improves human preference and prompt adherence across modalities and architectures; Juggernaut-XL achieves 90% HPSv2 winning rate over baseline.

problem: Multivariate time series forecasting methods overfit channel ordering (channel-dependent) or ignore inter-channel dependencies (channel-independent), limiting adaptability.
approach: CPiRi framework uses permutation-invariant regularization with spatio-temporal decoupling, freezing temporal encoder and learning content-driven inter-channel relations via channel shuffling.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art results, remains stable under channel reordering, and generalizes to unseen channels even with half-channel training.

problem: Multinomial logistic regression requires discrete output classes, limiting applicability to continuous-valued neural decoding tasks like time, orientation, or spatial position.
approach: Continuous MLR generalizes MLR to continuous output spaces via exponential-family conditional density estimation, mapping neural activity to probability densities over external covariates with GP-prior tuning functions.
contribution: Consistently outperforms DNNs, XGBoost, and FlexCode on mouse/monkey visual cortex, hippocampus, and motor cortex, enabling interpretable multimodal neural decoding.

problem: Federated learning degrades under real-world data heterogeneity with distribution shifts across clients and drifts over time, especially with unknown cluster structure.
approach: Feroma uses compact client distribution profiles to guide adaptive similarity-weighted model aggregation and test-time model assignment without prior knowledge of clients' data.
contribution: Improves accuracy up to 12 percentage points over baselines across 6 benchmarks while maintaining computational and communication overhead comparable to FedAvg.

problem: Vision-language models like CLIP struggle with query-based image retrieval when queries have unseen styles (sketches, artworks, low-resolution), failing under distribution shift.
approach: Hystar uses hypernetworks to generate per-query singular-value perturbations for attention layers, with static offsets on MLPs for stability, and StyleNCE loss emphasizing hard cross-style negatives.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on multi-style retrieval and cross-style classification while remaining parameter-efficient and stable.

problem: Classical VLMs autoregress tokens in surface-level vocabulary, suffering from inefficiency and missing semantic abstraction crucial for generation tasks.
approach: VL-JEPA predicts continuous embeddings of target texts via Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture, using frozen pretrained temporal encoder and lightweight selective decoding.
contribution: Achieves stronger performance than token-space VLMs with 50% fewer parameters; supports selective decoding reducing operations 2.85x; matches classical VLMs on VQA despite 1.6B parameter size.

problem: Projection-based debiasing in VLMs removes subspaces for known concepts but can amplify unintended biases in unconsidered concepts.
approach: WRING rotates embeddings within relevant subspaces rather than projecting them away, preserving relations to unconsidered concepts while addressing known biases.
contribution: Mitigates unintended bias amplification while debiasing vision-language models for known spurious correlations.

problem: Embodied AI systems struggle with spatial reasoning across diverse task demands and fail to enforce physical robot constraints, producing infeasible plans.
approach: OmniEVA uses task-adaptive 3D grounding via gated router and embodiment-aware reasoning loop incorporating goals and physical constraints, with dynamic feature injection.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on 7 of 8 embodied reasoning benchmarks; excels in object navigation and mobile manipulation.

problem: Concept erasure techniques for diffusion models fail on visual autoregressive models due to their next-scale token prediction paradigm, creating safety gaps.
approach: S-VARE uses filtered cross-entropy loss to identify minimal unsafe visual tokens, preservation loss for semantic fidelity, and auxiliary visual tokens reducing fine-tuning intensity.
contribution: Achieves surgical concept erasure in VAR while preserving generation quality and diversity.

problem: Brain tumor segmentation with missing MRI modalities loses crucial shared information using parallel fusion, degrading performance and generalization.
approach: SMSN uses sequential information bottleneck fusion to preserve shared information, sequentially extracting modality-common features and reconstructing modality-specific features.
contribution: Outperforms parallel fusion baselines on BRATS18/20 with diverse missing-modality robustness; achieves cross-domain generalization to brain metastasis without fine-tuning.

problem: Simulating strongly coupled multiphysics systems is challenging; mainstream approaches struggle with decoupled data and suffer from low efficiency and fidelity.
approach: GenCP formulates coupled-physics modeling as probability modeling, integrating probability density evolution in generative modeling with iterative multiphysics coupling via operator-splitting theory.
contribution: Demonstrates principled error controllability and superior performance on synthetic and challenging multiphysics scenarios (fluid-structure, thermal-flow coupling).

problem: Sequential disentanglement methods struggle with real-world multimodal data and lack established evaluation protocols for assessing representation learning.
approach: DiffSDA leverages diffusion models, latent diffusion, efficient samplers and a challenging evaluation protocol to separate static/dynamic factors across diverse modalities without relying on multiple loss terms.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art on time series, video, and audio benchmarks with modal-agnostic framework.

problem: Achieving high-fidelity, view-consistent renderings from point clouds without per-scene optimization remains a core challenge for novel view synthesis.
approach: DiffPBR uses diffusion models with viewpoint-projected noise constrained by scene geometry, adaptive CoNo-Splatting for fast rasterization, and residual learning in neural re-rendering.
contribution: Improves rendered image quality by 3-5dB, reduces GPU training from 41 to 8 hours, and increases rendering speed from 3.6fps to 10fps (one-step).

problem: Low-Rank Adaptation has fixed-rank design limiting flexibility; dynamic rank allocation methods lack principled matrix-wise granularity and capacity expansion mechanisms.
approach: FlexLoRA uses spectral energy entropy for matrix importance, supports rank pruning/expansion under global budget, and employs zero-impact initialization for stability.
contribution: Consistently outperforms state-of-the-art PEFT baselines via principled dynamic rank allocation.

problem: Molecular graph generation at atom-level is inefficient and limits property control; benchmarks lack evaluation of drug-discovery-relevant generation capabilities.
approach: FragFM performs fragment-level discrete flow matching with coarse-to-fine autoencoder reconstruction; introduces NPGen benchmark for natural product generation evaluation.
contribution: Achieves better property control than atom-based methods with flexible fragment conditioning; superior performance on diverse molecular benchmarks including NPGen.

problem: Preference models exhibit systematic miscalibration, overrelying on superficial patterns like length and style rather than substantive qualities, leading to reward hacking.
approach: Uses counterfactual data augmentation (CDA) with synthesized contrastive examples to fine-tune preference models, mitigating bias toward length, structure, jargon, sycophancy, and vagueness.
contribution: Reduces average miscalibration from 39.4% to 32.5% through simple post-training CDA.

problem: RL training lacks explicit critique or reflection mechanisms for improving reasoning and code generation capabilities.
approach: Critique-Coder combines standard RL and Critique Reinforcement Learning (CRL), where 20% of data is replaced with CRL tasks rewarding correct judgment of solution quality.
contribution: Consistently outperforms RL-only baselines; Critique-Coder-8B reaches over 60% on LiveCodeBench (v5), matching or exceeding reasoning models.

problem: VLA models sacrifice reasoning flexibility for manipulation performance and suffer catastrophic forgetting of pre-trained vision-language capabilities.
approach: InstructVLA preserves VLM reasoning via mixture-of-experts adaptation on both standard VLM corpora and 650K-sample VLA-IT dataset supporting multimodal instruction tuning.
contribution: Achieves 33.3% improvement over SpatialVLA on SimplerEnv; 96% over fine-tuned OpenVLA on SimplerEnv-Instruct; supports inference-time scaling via textual reasoning.

problem: Base language models often lack cognitive skills like verification, backtracking, and retrying that reasoning models use; distillation from stronger models is expensive.
approach: SkillFactory rearranges model's own samples to create training data in skill formats during SFT, priming models to acquire skills during RL without external model distillation.
contribution: Improves generalization to harder task variants post-RL; demonstrates robust cognitive skill use; RLed SkillFactory models resist out-of-domain regression better than RLed baselines.

problem: Masked diffusion models generate fixed-length sequences, unable to support variable-length token insertions crucial for flexible sequence generation.
approach: FlexMDMs extend masked diffusion via stochastic interpolant framework, generating sequences by inserting and unmasking tokens while provably retaining any-order inference.
contribution: Matches MDM perplexity with superior length fidelity; 60% higher maze planning success rate; retrofitted pretrained LLaDA-8B achieves 58%→67% on GSM8K, 52%→65% on code infilling.

problem: Modern neural sequence models balance parallelizable training and sequential inference via state space models, yet their full generality and expressivity remain characterizable.
approach: Defines Prefix-Scannable Models (PSMs) generalizing state space models to support arbitrary (non-associative) aggregation operators like softmax, unifying RNNs and linear transformers.
contribution: PSMs achieve O(1) amortized compute per token and log(N) memory while retaining transformer expressivity; show better length generalization than transformers or SSMs on benchmarks.

problem: Pre-trained VLMs like CLIP face distribution shifts and novel tasks in real deployment, requiring continual learning without catastrophic forgetting or replay buffers.
approach: NuSA-CL uses low-rank adaptation constrained to null space of current parameters, minimizing interference with prior knowledge via lightweight memory-free training.
contribution: Preserves zero-shot capabilities while achieving competitive continual learning performance with minimal computational and memory overhead.
theme: Transfer Learning, Meta Learning, and Lifelong Learning

problem: Label noise in binary classification degrades learning; instance-only dependent noise models are underutilized despite offering flexible estimation.
approach: Uses loss correction for instance-aware schema completing the bridge from noisy to clean risk minimization under classification calibration, enabling efficient transition rate estimation.
contribution: Demonstrates generalization across image, audio, tabular domains with neural networks and gradient-boosted machines via principled loss correction.

problem: Robots lack demonstrations for complex manipulation tasks (pouring, wiping, mixing); obtaining real demonstrations is expensive and task-specific.
approach: RIGVid generates video demonstrations via diffusion model, filters with VLM for command adherence, extracts 6D trajectories via pose tracking, and retargets to robot embodiment.
contribution: Filtered generated videos as effective as real demonstrations; performance improves with generation quality; outperforms compact alternatives like VLM keypoint prediction.

problem: LLM representational spaces lack interpretability regarding learned information, limiting understanding of how models learn and relating them to human learning.
approach: Frames LLM training as lossy compression via Information Bottleneck, showing models approach compression bounds for next-sequence prediction while compressing differently per training recipe.
contribution: Demonstrates compression structure predicts downstream MMLU-Pro performance, linking representational structure to actionable performance insights across LLM families.

problem: Muon optimizer outperforms Adam in LLM training, yet underlying mechanisms remain unclear, hindering principled optimizer development.
approach: Analyzes Muon through associative memory lens, revealing VO attention and FFN optimization as primary contributors; explains superiority via isotropic singular spectra enabling balanced tail-class learning.
contribution: Theoretically confirms Muon achieves balanced cross-class learning on heavy-tailed data unlike Adam, explaining real-world corpus performance gap.

problem: Deep reinforcement learning suffers from sample inefficiency despite advances in model architecture and algorithms; optimization landscape properties remain underexplored.
approach: XQC combines batch normalization, weight normalization, and distributional cross-entropy loss to achieve orders-of-magnitude-smaller critic Hessian condition numbers, with gradient norm bounding.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art sample efficiency across 55 proprioception and 15 vision-based tasks using significantly fewer parameters than competing methods.
